first_error_evidence: Step 7: agent used 'tmux split-window -h' to create what it intended as a top/bottom split, but -h in tmux creates a left/right (vertical divider) split. The task required a top pane with two bottom panes, so the pane layout was incorrect from the start.
near_miss_description: The tmux pane layout was never corrected to the specified top/bottom-then-split-bottom arrangement. The agent ran all scripts in the wrong panes. However, the bug fix (adding strip() to line.strip().split(',')) was ultimately applied correctly at step 23 after two failed intermediate attempts, and the functional output was correct.
near_miss_evidence: Steps 7-8 established a left/right layout instead of top/bottom. The agent never corrected this. Steps 18 and 22 revealed that earlier fixes (vim edit in step 14, sed in steps 20-21) were all incorrect and corrupted the file. Only at step 23 did the agent fully rewrite the file correctly. Output at step 25 showed clean CSV without double newlines.
verification_evidence: Steps 24-26: agent ran the script directly (not via tmux), observed 'Completed. Processed 9 records.', then verified output.csv showed no extra blank lines (step 25), and checked process.log entries (step 26) before claiming completion at step 27.
suspicious_pass_evidence: The tmux pane layout specified in the task (top monitor pane, bottom-left process pane, bottom-right editor pane) was never correctly established. The agent used -h instead of -v for the initial split, creating left/right panes instead of top/bottom. The evaluation apparently accepted the result despite this structural deviation, possibly because the evaluation checked the functional outcome (bug fixed, correct output) rather than strict tmux layout conformance.
one_sentence_strategy_summary: The agent explored the project files, set up an incorrectly-arranged tmux layout, attempted to fix a newline bug via vim (corrupting the file), then made two failed sed repair attempts before correctly rewriting the entire process_data.py from scratch and verifying clean output.
